blockers.issue: POST /materialize is publicly reachable through the deployed /api/odyssey/ nginx proxy and has no auth, allowlist, rate limit, quota, CSRF protection, or per-request cost guard. Because it invokes runAgent and paid Tavily/LLM/fetch work on cache misses, anyone can burn API spend by POSTing uncached names or free-text inputs. The deployment script confirms a public proxy to 127.0.0.1:18792 and only smoke-tests the public origin; it does not add auth.

Citation provenance is not enforced on the final persisted citation set. validateForEmit checks payload.citations only, but canonicalize later calls normalizeCitations(next.citations, next.sources), so an emitted payload can pass with one grounded citation while arbitrary ungrounded URLs in sources/link/href entries are persisted as citations.

fetchedUrls is populated by recursively scanning the entire fetch_page tool result. That includes the untrusted page markdown, not just the actual fetched URL in details/url or the untrusted_page wrapper URL. A fetched page that merely mentions or links to another URL can therefore make that URL pass the 'actually fetched or search result' citation gate.

The loadPending shared-promise and runLocked cleanup fixes are present, but pending reverse persistence is still not serialized. Concurrent cache.write calls can mutate pendingReverses and set pendingDirty while another flushPending is between atomicWriteJson and pendingDirty=false; the earlier flush can then clear the dirty flag for a later mutation that was not included in its serialized file, losing pending reverse updates on disk.

Disambiguator support exists for makeSlug and the current node, but edge targets still cannot carry disambiguators through canonicalization or frontier expansion. normalizeEdge recomputes edge slugs from only type/name, and enqueueEdges queues AgentInput with only type/name, so two distinct same-name targets are still collapsed before either materialization can preserve identity.

warnings.issue: The materialize validator accepts a body with a valid type but no name and no text, despite the API contract saying {type, name} or {text}. That sends a vague type-only prompt into runAgent and compounds the public cost-exhaustion risk.

Same structured slug requests are coalesced, but free-text requests are not. Two different prompts can materialize to the same canonical slug, both pay the JIT cost, and cache.write is atomic at the file-rename level but not write-if-absent under the slug lock, so the last writer can win.

The local fetcher is now the default and wraps output in untrusted_page, but JSDOM/Readability/Turndown errors are not caught with a fallback path. The 10s timeout is also cleared after response headers, before res.text(), and there is no max response-byte cap, so pathological HTML or slow/huge bodies can fail or stall a materialization until the outer agent timeout.

The deploy path hardcodes nginx to port 18792 while src/server.ts defaults to 18791 unless PORT is present. /etc/odyssey-music.env is written chmod 600, which is good, but the service runs as root and the port coupling is fragile if the env file is missing or the service is launched outside systemd.
npm run check exits successfully, but Biome reports nodesWithMetrics as an unused variable in scripts/analytics.ts.
AgentDeps.maxEmitAttempts still has a stale comment saying the Nth attempt accepts best-effort payloads. Runtime behavior now hard-aborts, but the public interface documentation is misleading.

summary: FAIL: Many claimed fixes are present: slug.ts accepts a disambiguator for direct slug generation; validateForEmit splits search/fetch counters; abandon_node has guard rails; maxEmitAttempts now hard-aborts instead of accepting best effort; Firecrawl, Tavily, and local fetch output are wrapped in untrusted boundaries; local fetch is the default; crawler claimed reservation and release logic plus bfs/popularity/hybrid strategies are implemented; loadPending sharing and runLocked cleanup are implemented; schemas add per-edge target constraints and _metrics; server endpoints exist with in-flight coalescing for exact structured slugs; analytics/coverage scripts exist; and cache/ is tracked. Existing checks run: npm run check passed with one Biome warning, and scripts/assert-cache.ts cache 2000 passed. Blockers remain around the unauthenticated public JIT endpoint, citation provenance bypasses, pending reverse flush concurrency, and missing disambiguator propagation for edge/frontier targets.
